answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity costly to fake: a new agent must lock a refundable deposit at a single vertex of the trust graph, and only earns it back after peers attest real completed work. Like a trellis, those attestations link agents into a visible web, so a flood of fresh, unconnected clones stands out. A harbor rule then caps how many newcomers one sponsor can vouch for per epoch, so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than any spam run can recover.
